sections.html:
Gallatin is the seat of Sumner County, on the Cumberland River about 30 miles northeast of Nashville. Growth has been quick: 44,431 residents in 2020, then 54,590 by the July 2025 estimate, which is 22.8 percent more.

The middle owner-occupied house is valued at $372,000 across 2020 to 2024, slightly higher than the national $332,700. Monthly owner costs at the median are $1,778 with a loan and $552 with none, while the median rent is $1,395. Owners hold 57.1 percent of the city's 19,755 households, and household income at the median is $77,518.

Getting around is easy to describe to a buyer. US 31E, also called Nashville Pike or Gallatin Road, is the main street, and State Route 386 is a controlled-access road that ends in Gallatin and ties into Interstate 65. A daily WeGo Public Transit bus runs to downtown Nashville. The county school board runs the public schools, and Gallatin High, Station Camp High and Liberty Creek High are the high schools.

Gallatin charges $0.5295 per $100 of assessed value for 2026, and the Sumner County assessor supplies the values. Interest begins March 1, so pay before then. State law leaves mailed notices optional, which means a missing bill gets you nowhere. Short on cash? The Recorder's Office can set up a payment plan.

Some owners get a break. Gallatin extends relief to qualifying elderly homeowners, disabled homeowners and disabled veteran or widow homeowners, and a tax freeze program exists too. The freeze has to be recertified every year with the Sumner County Trustee.

The county revalues property on a five-year cycle: 2024 was the last round and 2029 is next.

The cheapest first move is a phone call. Ask the assessor's office to look again at your value; many disagreements end there. Still unhappy? The county Board of Equalization takes appeals starting June 1. Beyond it sits the State Board, where you must file by August 1 or within 45 days of the local notice, whichever is later.

A lower assessment stays with the house, so winning before you list also helps your buyer. Bring photos of defects and sale prices of comparable nearby houses.

sections.h2: Who to call in Gallatin and Sumner County
sections.html:
Most seller errands lead to one of five offices.

Offices for common seller errands

Gallatin replaced its zoning ordinance and map as of September 1, 2026, so anything you remember about a lot's zoning is worth rechecking with Planning at 615-451-5796. That department also deals with fences, signs, temporary use permits and flood zone questions. Its planning commission and zoning appeals board move on a six-week review cycle, a wait to factor into any plan needing approval.

Apply for building permits in the city's Citizens Self-Service Portal. Contractors must email permits@gallatintn.gov with proof of a state license, general liability and workers' compensation insurance or a state exemption, and a signed city permit bond with a power of attorney before they can apply.

If a past owner finished the basement or built an addition, ask the permit office whether the permits were closed. Expect the buyer's lender and inspector to ask too.

sections.h2: Recording the deed in Sumner County
sections.html:
The Sumner County Register of Deeds, on North Belvedere Drive, files every Gallatin deed. Hours are 8 to 4:30 on weekdays, and a normal year brings in over 30,000 documents. Simplifile and CSC handle electronic filing. MyLandAlert, a free notice service, will email you if anything is recorded under your name.

The state conveyance tax is gathered by the register: 37 cents on each $100 of price, owed by the grantee. Online searching is available, certified records start in September 1989, and the digitized deed books and indexes reach back to 1786.

sections.h2: Moving fast: what changes with a cash sale
sections.html:
Three questions come before everything else: what do you still owe the lender, is any tax outstanding, and whose names are on the deed? When an heir is selling, have a title company follow the recorded chain of deeds before anyone picks a date, because a gap in it can freeze a closing for weeks.

A buyer with a mortgage must clear loan approval and an appraisal, either of which can push the deal back toward repairs or a lower price. Cash buyers avoid both, leaving title work as the main clock. If you are leaving soon, get the closing date in writing and make sure the tax bill, and any city payment plan balance, comes out of the sale proceeds.

Hand these to the title company before you accept an offer:

  • the newest city and county tax bills
  • permit records for any basement or room an earlier owner added
  • a payoff letter if a loan is still open

sections.h2: Selling an inherited or problem house
sections.html:
Heirs and owners living elsewhere sell in Gallatin regularly, and they tend to hit the same snags. The deed comes first. The Register of Deeds can tell you who is on record, and a title company can follow earlier transfers through the books. When the name on the deed belongs to a deceased parent, the title company will want estate papers before it insures a buyer.

Then tour the house with permits in mind. An old basement finish or bedroom addition may have no closed permit, and a lender's inspector usually spots it. An early call to the city permit office gives you time to choose: close the permit, price around it or sell to someone who takes the house as it stands.

Last, review the tax side. Request the city bill and the county bill separately, since two offices issue them, and ask about the freeze or relief programs if the owner qualified. Any unpaid balance gets cleared at closing, so learning the number first spares everyone a surprise on the settlement statement.

Count backward from the day you must be out. A listing runs through photos, showings, an offer, the buyer's inspection, an appraisal and loan approval, with delay possible at each stage. A cash sale shrinks the list to an offer, a title search and a closing, which is why owners on a deadline lean toward it. The tax and deed calls above are needed either way, so make them this week.

faqs.a: About 54,590 in the July 2025 estimate, a 22.8 percent increase over the 44,431 counted in 2020.

faqs.q: What is the City of Gallatin property tax rate?
faqs.a: For 2026 the city charges $0.5295 per $100 of assessed value, and interest begins March 1 on any unpaid balance.

faqs.q: When did Gallatin's new zoning ordinance take effect?
faqs.a: September 1, 2026. Planning, at 615-451-5796, can tell you how a specific lot is zoned under the new map.

faqs.q: How do I dispute my Sumner County property value?
faqs.a: Ask the assessor, at 615-452-2412, for an informal review first. If the number still seems wrong, take it to the county Board of Equalization, which meets starting June 1.

faqs.q: Which office files the deed on a Gallatin house?
faqs.a: Sumner County's Register of Deeds handles it, in Suite 201 at 355 N. Belvedere Dr. Call 615-452-3892. Simplifile and CSC carry electronic filings.
